open_points.subject: Randomly minted record identities
open_points.text: `trial_execution_id` M07, `binding_id` M11, `run_id` M19, `approval_id` M24 and `grant_id` M25 are minted at random by the kernel; one that already exists is minted again.
open_points.question: Which module owns random-ID generation, collision detection and repeated minting for these records?
options: `store` mints and collision-checks every random identity inside the creating transaction
Each record-owning module mints identities and asks `store` to reject collisions
A new lower-level identity/randomness module owns minting and is used by the record-owning modules
open_points.default_guess: Have `store` mint and collision-check the identity atomically in the record-creation transaction.

open_points.subject: Port declaration validation shared by contracts and bindings
open_points.text: `functions` owns A02 ... contract versions with their ceilings check ... `bindings` owns A08 ... proposal checks ... or its ports break a rule A02 sets for contract ports
open_points.question: Which module owns the common predicate for port-name uniqueness, carriage/media-type consistency and supported-schema validity, given that `functions` and `bindings` are on the same dependency line and may not know each other?
options: `canonical_values` owns a reusable port-declaration validator consumed by both modules
`functions` owns the predicate and the dependency rule is relaxed so `bindings` may call it
`functions` and `bindings` independently implement the same rules, making both owners of the shared facts
open_points.default_guess: Put the reusable, context-parameterized port-declaration validation in `canonical_values`, with `functions` and `bindings` retaining their operation-specific ordering and class rules.
